title: San Francisco supervisors hit pause on new data centers amid AI boom
key_facts: San Francisco's Board of Supervisors approved a 45-day moratorium on approving new data centers this week.
Supervisor Shamann Walton sponsored it; planning officials must report back within 25 days on defining data centers and studying energy, water, air quality, land use and community effects.
Oakland's City Council adopted its own 45-day moratorium on Tuesday; Gilroy did in mid-September.
Walton says some data centers were approved under 2001 'Internet Service Exchange' rules; they cluster in Bayview and South of Market.
San Francisco Planning says only two new data centers have been approved since 2002 and none is pending.
Walton says New York enacted a statewide moratorium in July; about eight California bills are under consideration.
Business group GrowSF called the proposal 'importing a national political panic' and said water and power concerns are overblown.
quote_evidence: “We cannot use 2001 rules to regulate 2026 technology,” Walton said.
The City has no current pending applications to develop any new data centers, Hannan said.
why_it_matters_hint: A growing list of cities is pausing data center approvals.
